content:
This page gathers the questions people ask most about Paul and gives each a short answer, with a link to the article that holds the full evidence. Each answer rests on Paul's own letters and on the Acts of the Apostles. Claims that missionaries make in his defence are answered in [paulus_link slug="answers" /], and an overview of his life is in [paulus_link slug="paul-at-a-glance" /]. Behind every question is one: what Paul made of the message of ʿĪsā ibn Maryam (ʿalayhi al-salām, peace be upon him).

Who was Paul?

A Jew of Tarsus, first called Saul, who persecuted the followers of ʿĪsā ibn Maryam and then claimed to be their apostle. He is the main figure of the second half of Acts, and thirteen letters of the New Testament carry his name.

Full answer: [paulus_link slug="who-was-paul-of-tarsus" /]

Are Saul and Paul one man?

Yes. Saul was his Hebrew name and Paul his Roman one. Acts uses Saul until Cyprus, "Then Saul, (who also is called Paul,)", and Paul after. He is not King Saul, who reigned a thousand years earlier.

Full answer: [paulus_link slug="the-roman" /] and [paulus_link slug="saul-in-the-bible" /]

The meaning of his names

Paul is the Latin Paulus, "small". Saul is the Hebrew Shaʾul, "asked for". In Arabic he is Būlus.

Full answer: [paulus_link slug="meaning-of-the-name-paul" /]

Birth, tribe and appearance

Born in Tarsus in Cilicia, of the tribe of Benjamin (Philippians 3:5), probably in the first decade of the first century. The only early witness to his looks is an opponent, who said that "his bodily presence is weak".

Full answer: [paulus_link slug="tarsus-and-a-persona-for-every-audience" /] and [paulus_link slug="paul-in-the-churches" /]

Did he have a wife?

Not when he wrote 1 Corinthians: he wished that all men were "even as I myself". Whether he had married earlier is unknown.

Full answer: [paulus_link slug="was-paul-married" /]

Jew, Pharisee or Gentile?

A Jew and a Pharisee, by his own words: "an Hebrew of the Hebrews; as touching the law, a Pharisee". He later spoke of Judaism as his religion "in time past".

Full answer: [paulus_link slug="who-was-paul-of-tarsus" /]

His Roman citizenship

Acts says he was a citizen by birth (Acts 22:28). His own letters never say so, and he was beaten with rods three times (2 Corinthians 11:25), a punishment citizens were spared.

Full answer: [paulus_link slug="the-citizenship-and-the-appeal-to-caesar" /]

Did he sit on the Sanhedrin?

No source says so. When he told Agrippa "I gave my voice against them", the Greek speaks of a pebble or vote, which may mean no more than his approval.

Full answer: [paulus_link slug="saul-the-persecutor" /]

Paul and Jesus: did they meet?

Not in Jesus's life on earth. Paul claims one meeting, a vision after the crucifixion, and he is its only witness.

Full answer: [paulus_link slug="did-paul-ever-meet-jesus" /]

Paul and the Twelve

He was not one of them. The eleven chose Matthias to replace Judas (Acts 1:26), and Paul set himself apart from "the twelve" in his own list of witnesses.

Full answer: [paulus_link slug="a-self-appointed-apostle" /]

His teachers

Acts says he studied under Gamaliel (Acts 22:3). Paul says his gospel came from no man: "neither was I taught it, but by the revelation of Jesus Christ".

Full answer: [paulus_link slug="a-self-appointed-apostle" /]

Saul before Damascus

He persecuted the church, by his own account, "beyond measure". Acts puts him at the stoning of Stephen and has him drag believers to prison.

Full answer: [paulus_link slug="saul-the-persecutor" /]

The road to Damascus

Acts tells of a light, a voice and three days of blindness, and tells it three times with differences. Paul's letters describe a revelation, with no road and no fall.

Full answer: [paulus_link slug="the-damascus-road" /] and [paulus_link slug="the-three-accounts-compared" /]

His death

The Bible does not record it. Tradition from about 200 CE says he was beheaded in Rome under Nero, about 64 to 67, at about sixty years of age.

Full answer: [paulus_link slug="a-death-the-scriptures-never-record" /]

Paul and the origins of the church

The evidence points to Paul as the founder of the religion that took Christ's name: its earliest books, its Gentile mission and its doctrines are his.

Full answer: [paulus_link slug="paul-the-father-of-a-new-religion" /]

His journeys and preaching

Acts records three journeys through Cyprus, Asia Minor and Greece, and a voyage to Rome as a prisoner. His letters add Arabia and Illyricum.

Full answer: [paulus_link slug="pauls-missionary-journeys" /] and [paulus_link slug="chronology" /]

Arrests and imprisonments

Acts records his jailing at Philippi, his arrest in Jerusalem, two years at Caesarea and two in Rome. Paul claims "in prisons more frequent" than his rivals, and 1 Clement says seven.

Full answer: [paulus_link slug="chronology" /]

His letters

Thirteen letters carry his name; scholars accept seven as his. Hebrews is anonymous, and Acts is Luke's.

Full answer: [paulus_link slug="paul-and-the-new-testament" /] and [paulus_link slug="the-letters-of-a-man" /]

His teaching

Justification by faith without the works of the law, an atoning death, and Christ as Son and Lord.

Full answer: [paulus_link slug="seven-doctrines" /] and [paulus_link slug="pauls-own-titles" /]

Was he real?

Yes. His letters are among the oldest Christian writings, and 1 Clement names him within a generation of his death. What is disputed is how far his account of himself can be trusted.

Full answer: [paulus_link slug="who-was-paul-of-tarsus" /] and [paulus_link slug="the-character-of-paul" /]

What Muslim scholars said of him

The Qurʾān does not name him. Muslim scholars who studied his teaching judged him the corrupter of the religion of ʿĪsā ibn Maryam.

Full answer: [paulus_link slug="paul-in-the-islamic-tradition" /] and [paulus_link slug="the-early-islamic-record" /]

The Gentile mission

Paul gave himself the title: "I am the apostle of the Gentiles". ʿĪsā ibn Maryam, by Matthew's account, was sent to Israel.

Full answer: [paulus_link slug="apostle-to-the-gentiles" /]

The thorn in the flesh

Paul does not say what it was: "a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me". Eyesight, malaria and epilepsy are guesses.

Full answer: [paulus_link slug="ego-epilepsy-and-narcissism" /] and [paulus_link slug="the-flesh" /]

Rumours about his private life

No source supports them. What he taught about the body and desire is another matter.

Full answer: [paulus_link slug="the-flesh" /]

Paul and the teaching of ʿĪsā ibn Maryam

Paul cites sayings of Jesus only a few times, and the community led by James ruled against his gospel.

Full answer: [paulus_link slug="paul-against-the-disciples" /] and [paulus_link slug="james-the-brother" /]

The case against him

Six counts, each with its own articles and references.

Full answer: [paulus_link slug="the-charges" /]
